how-assert-works: The Canine Resource Center is open: the documentation, guides, essays and whitepapers behind Assert, Assay, Assure and the engine under them, in one place. Every article carries its version, the date it was signed and who signed it. Start with how Assert works and the reading route through it.
findings-count-is-not-depth: We once briefed a 10 to 20 times findings claim as evidence of depth. Measured across the corpus it was 0.86 to 1.29 times. This essay is what we withdrew, and the instrument we replaced it with.
what-a-false-positive-actually-is: Every scanner claims a low false-positive rate, because nobody agrees what counts as one. The five classes we adjudicate every finding into, and how to read anyone's number, ours included.
read-only-by-design: A surveyor that also edits the thing it grades has a conflict it cannot audit away. What happens to your source code during an Assert scan, and the single opt-in exception to read-only.
autonomy-levels-are-the-wrong-question: Every published autonomy ladder for coding agents runs out at the rung where continuous agents actually operate. Why the ladder is the wrong question, and what to ask instead.
which-scanner-should-i-buy-first: Which scanner to buy first depends on which classes of check your pipeline already enforces. That is a fact about your repository, not about the market. How to read it from your own code.
a-dependency-matrix-shows-cycles-not-lay: A mark above the diagonal of a dependency matrix is a cycle, exactly that and nothing more. Why an architecturally wrong dependency can sit below it, and the correction we had to make in our own reading.
architecture-you-cannot-draw-by-hand: Most dependency graphs stop at the edge of one ecosystem's build files. Read from a language-neutral code model, the same question is answerable across the whole product, whatever the languages.
survey-clarity-is-not-language-quality: Language support is not binary. The two kinds we publish per language, why TypeScript and JavaScript are not the same claim, and what our 0 to 10 number does and does not say.
what-not-fixing-it-costs: A fix has a cost. Not doing it also has a cost, paid on every change to the same code. What is measured, what is assumed, and when the model refuses to answer.
the-fix-you-should-do-first-is-not-the-b: The same fix is worth more on code the team edits every week than on code nobody has opened in three years. Why change frequency belongs in the ranking, and why it is bounded.
what-a-score-is-for: A single number is worthless as a verdict and valuable as a comparison. Why the rubric is frozen, why the weakest area pulls the headline down, and how much of a move is worth acting on.
a-number-you-can-re-derive: A score is only evidence if a third party can recompute it from the same inputs and get the same answer. What has to travel with the number, and four questions to ask of any score you are shown.
what-technical-due-diligence-misses: A fortnight of reading produces a snapshot and an opinion. Three limits that come from the format of technical due diligence, not from the people doing it, and what a re-derivable verdict adds.
a-rebuild-range-is-not-a-valuation: What it would cost to rebuild a codebase is bounded and can be modelled. What the business is worth cannot. Why the figure is always a range, and the framings it is given in.
ten-questions-for-any-code-benchmark: Most published code benchmarks can be judged in two minutes, before you read a single result. Ten questions to ask, turned on our own work first.
does-a-maintainability-score-agree-with-: We scored the 304 public classes that independent professionals had rated, under an analysis fixed before we looked. The score agrees with the experts. File length agrees almost as well, and the essay says what that means.
does-the-shape-of-a-codebase-change-what: The same 20 methods, fixed by the same agent before and after we split our engine into slices. After the split it cost 1.86 times as many tokens. What we measured and how.
a-gate-an-agent-cannot-talk-its-way-past: We moved fourteen detectors off model judgement. Twelve of them failed their first adjudication against the code. What a gate has to be for an agent not to talk its way past it.
ten-repositories-wrote-half-the-result: In one of our own measurement cycles, 9 of 268 repositories carried half of all noise rows. A percentage over rows is partly a fact about the sample. How we rank instead.
your-agent-says-it-is-fixed: On our own code, about one in seven fixes a coding agent reported as done was not: the next scan still found the problem. Why the check has to come from outside the agent.
from-alert-volume-to-evidence: Whitepaper: a practical standard for evaluating code-analysis claims. How to move a conversation about scanners from alert volume to evidence a buyer can check.
beyond-the-language-logo: Whitepaper: what supported means for a language in our engine. Capabilities, limits, fitness and validation, as published in the language catalogue rather than as a logo on a slide.
from-measurement-to-verifiable-delivery: Whitepaper: recomputable scoring and signed provenance. How a measurement of code becomes a delivery the buyer can verify without trusting the supplier or us.
the-code-remembers: Whitepaper: prioritising maintainability risk from repository history. The code remembers where the team spends its time, and that belongs in the order of the work.
paid-to-measure-never-to-move-the-number: Whitepaper: how our commercial model keeps the verdict out of every price. Prices that never depend on the score, no remediation revenue, and a firewall enforced in the build.
a-different-unit-of-judgement: Whitepaper: the codebase survey beside your scanners. Why a judgement about a whole codebase is a different unit from a list of alerts, and what it adds to the tools you already run.
how-the-code-assurance-index-is-construc: Whitepaper: how the Code Assurance Index is constructed. Ten lenses, an ordered weighting, and the firewall that keeps advisory findings out of the score.
assessing-ai-assisted-code: Whitepaper: an artifact-first framework for evidence-linked code-health assessment of AI-assisted code. What to measure when the author is partly an agent.
the-engine-measured: Whitepaper: what our own findings are worth, measured on a held-out corpus we drew before we looked.
noise-is-two-dimensional: Whitepaper: a single noise rate has one coordinate too few. How many it needs, and what changes when a scanner's noise is reported that way.
